issue: Main pushes fail CI OK when Clippy is skipped under verified reuse because the nested selector is missing from the proof.
resolution: Moved runner selection out of the reusable workflow so the gate can match the Clippy job in the merge-queue proof. The first main push after the fix verified reuse and passed CI OK.

issue: The capacity snapshot does not reserve a runner. Dell jobs waited up to 48 minutes 47 seconds after selection in the 50-run sample.
resolution: Clud now reserves a runner through the broker and falls back to hosted Ubuntu after a denial or missed readiness deadline. Both branches passed in live CI. One granted reservation expired while Docker spent 100.7 seconds starting the runner on FSX3MN2. The host reported high disk I/O pressure during that start. Its dispatcher polls the broker in a separate worker, and the underlying Docker startup latency remains a host-level limit.

issue: Four Linux unit test shards ran after the Dell build failed and tried to download its missing bundle.
resolution: Require the Linux build to finish successfully before its unit test consumers start.

issue: A Dell build failed after losing the connection to its Soldr cache daemon.
resolution: Retry compilation once through Soldr with its compiler cache disabled after the known disconnect. This avoids the failing connection on the retry. The original daemon exit has no confirmed host-side cause.

issue: The CI docs name a retired routing label and imply the runner group only serves clud. The live label is clud-linux-x64. The 50-run sample had 76 Dell build and Clippy assignments, all on FSX3MN2, with 75 successful jobs.
resolution: Document the live fleet observation, the routing switch, and the reservation and rollback behavior.

issue: A same-commit Dell build ran 8m02s longer than its hosted counterpart. The Dell run missed the build cache and the hosted run restored a partial cache.
resolution: All four Clud slot locks are now runner-owned. A reserved Dell run logged 570 compiler cache hits and 8 misses, then saved a new local dependency archive. A later reservation on the same slot restored 4,840 files and skipped the full dependency cook. The warm Dell build took 709 seconds after a 96-second selector job. The hosted build of the same tree took 731 seconds after a 14-second selector job. Workflow events and cache states differed. Hosted-to-Dell path parity remains tracked upstream.

issue: Uploading the Linux test bundle took a median 153s on Dell and 3s on GitHub-hosted. The same-commit jobs uploaded nearly identical byte counts.
resolution: Verified-reuse main CI passed on Dell with both artifact steps skipped. A Dell queue build published a zstd bundle 19.4% smaller than the hosted gzip bundle from the same tree, and all four hosted test jobs unpacked it and passed. The compressed upload still took 130 seconds. The Dell and workstation shared a public IPv4 address and each uploaded 16 MiB of synthetic data to Cloudflare at roughly 8 to 11 Mbit/s. The Dell reached 514 Mbit/s over the LAN. The measurements point to a shared internet upload constraint. Locating the limiting link requires gateway or provider telemetry.
